greek: Καὶ ἐξάρας Ιακωβ τοὺς πόδας ἐπορεύθη εἰς γῆν ἀνατολῶν πρὸς Λαβαν τὸν υἱὸν Βαθουηλ τοῦ Σύρου ἀδελφὸν δὲ Ρεβεκκας μητρὸς Ιακωβ καὶ Ησαυ.
hint: Jacob lifted his feet and went to the land of the east, to Laban son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah the mother of Jacob and Esau.

notes.text: The Hebrew idiom *wayyiśśāʾ raglāyw*, *he lifted his feet*, carried over word for word.
Middle Liddell heads the entry with the Epic ἐξαείρω.

names.gloss: (Ιακωβ, from Hebrew Yaʿăqōb, which the Hebrew of 25:26 hears in ʿāqēb, "heel")
(Βαθουηλ, from Hebrew Bĕtûʾēl, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ ὁρᾷ καὶ ἰδοὺ φρέαρ ἐν τῷ πεδίῳ, ἦσαν δὲ ἐκεῖ τρία ποίμνια προβάτων ἀναπαυόμενα ἐπʼ αὐτοῦ· ἐκ γὰρ τοῦ φρέατος ἐκείνου ἐπότιζον τὰ ποίμνια, λίθος δὲ ἦν μέγας ἐπὶ τῷ στόματι τοῦ φρέατος,
hint: And he looks, and there is a well in the plain, and three flocks of sheep resting by it; for from that well they watered the flocks, and a great stone was on the mouth of the well.

notes.text: The present, in a past narrative: the historic present.
One sense, *a flock*; Middle Liddell's second, of disciples, glosses nothing.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό, *at the same place*.

hint: He said to them: Do you know Laban son of Nahor? And they said: We know him.

notes.text: Laban is Nahor's grandson; the Greek says *son*, as the Hebrew does.

hint: He said to them: Is he well? And they said: He is well. And here is Rachel his daughter coming with the sheep.

notes.text: The Hebrew is *hăšālôm lô*, *is there peace to him*; the Greek asks after his health.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus puts ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος before it, and adds the end of verse 9 here.

hint: And Jacob said: There is still much day, it is not yet time for the cattle to be gathered; water the sheep and go and pasture them.

hint: And he told Rachel that he was her father's brother and that he was Rebekah's son, and she ran and told her father these words.

reading: and [[collected|collected, gathered together, took up, laid hold of and seized, comprehended, conceived|συλλαμβάνω]] [[back|back, again, once more, over again|πάλιν]] [[name:Λεια]] and [[brought into the world|brought into the world, brought forth, bore, produced|τίκτω]] son [[second|second, next, inferior|δεύτερος]] to [[name:Ιακωβ]] and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[heard|heard, had hearing of, heard tell of, hearkened and gave ear, listened to and obeyed|ἀκούω]] [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over|κύριος]] [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[I am hated|I am hated|μισέω]], and [[gave besides|gave besides|προσδίδωμι]] to me also [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]]; [[called|called, summoned, called to himself, invited|καλέω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] of him [[name:Συμεων]].

greek: καὶ συνέλαβεν ἔτι καὶ ἔτεκεν υἱὸν καὶ εἶπεν Ἐν τῷ νῦν καιρῷ πρὸς ἐμοῦ ἔσται ὁ ἀνήρ μου, ἔτεκον γὰρ αὐτῷ τρεῖς υἱούς· διὰ τοῦτο ἐκάλεσεν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Λευι.
hint: And she conceived again and bore a son and said: In the present season my husband will be mine, for I have borne him three sons; therefore she called his name Levi.

notes.text: πρός with the genitive, *on my side*, of what belongs to one.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads τέτοκα, the perfect, and ἐκλήθη, *was called*, for ἐκάλεσεν.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[collected|collected, gathered together, took up, laid hold of and seized, comprehended, conceived|συλλαμβάνω]] [[yet|yet, as yet, still, further, besides, moreover|ἔτι]] and [[brought into the world|brought into the world, brought forth, bore, produced|τίκτω]] son and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[in the due measure|within, inside of, and by means of the due measure, the proportion, the fitness, the vital part, the right point of time, the proper time and season, the exact and critical time, the time, the advantage and profit and fruit|καιρός]] [[now|now, even now, just now|νῦν]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + genitive]] of me will be the [[the man|the man, the man in the prime of life|ἀνήρ]] of me, [[I brought into the world|I brought into the world, I brought forth, I bore, I produced|τίκτω]] for to him three sons; [[through|through, throughout and over, during, by aid of and by means of, by reason of, because of, for the sake of|διά + accusative]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[called|called, summoned, called to himself, invited|καλέω]] [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] of him [[name:Λευι]].

names.gloss: (Λευι, from Hebrew Lēwî, which the Hebrew of this verse hears in lāwâ, "he will be joined")

greek: καὶ συλλαβοῦσα ἔτι ἔτεκεν υἱὸν καὶ εἶπεν Νῦν ἔτι τοῦτο ἐξομολογήσομαι κυρίῳ· διὰ τοῦτο ἐκάλεσεν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ιουδα. καὶ ἔστη τοῦ τίκτειν.
hint: And she conceived again and bore a son and said: Now this time I will confess to the Lord; therefore she called his name Judah. And she stopped bearing.

notes.text: The Hebrew hears the name in *yādâ*, *praise, give thanks*, which the Greek keeps in ἐξομολογήσομαι.
ἵστημι in the intransitive aorist, with the articular infinitive: she stood off from bearing.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.
